Rover reaches the crater rim after a two-year traverse

By A. Writer, Example Portal

The rover arrived at the crater rim on Tuesday, the agency said in a briefing that lasted about an hour and covered the traverse in detail.

Engineers said the climb took longer than planned, because a stretch of loose sand forced the team to reroute twice, adding roughly four months to the schedule.

From the rim, the rover will photograph layered rock that scientists believe was laid down by standing water, the mission's project scientist told reporters.

  • Read more: How the rover picks its route over rough ground
  • Read more: The instruments on board and what each one measures

The next science campaign is scheduled to begin in the spring, once the team has finished a check of the rover's wheels and its sampling arm.
